lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Part 1. You will hear a man phoning a climbing centre to ask about courses for beginners. First, you have some time to look at questions 1 to 6.

lines.speaker: SOPHIE
lines.text: Good afternoon, Lakeside Climbing Centre, Sophie speaking. How can I help?

lines.speaker: MAN
lines.text: Oh, hello. I'm thinking of taking up climbing, and I wondered what courses you have for complete beginners.

lines.speaker: SOPHIE
lines.text: Well, most people start with one of our taster sessions. They last about two hours, and you get to try the main climbing wall with an instructor.

lines.speaker: MAN
lines.text: Do I need any experience at all?

lines.speaker: SOPHIE
lines.text: None at all. Most people on a taster have never climbed before, and some have never even been inside a climbing centre.

lines.speaker: MAN
lines.text: That sounds ideal. What exactly would I learn?

lines.speaker: SOPHIE
lines.text: The basics of climbing technique, and how to put on and use the harness safely. That's the most important thing on the first day.

lines.speaker: MAN
lines.text: And how big are the groups?

lines.speaker: SOPHIE
lines.text: We usually have about six people, but we never take more than eight, so the instructor can keep an eye on everyone.

lines.speaker: MAN
lines.text: Great. And what does it cost?

lines.speaker: SOPHIE
lines.text: It's twenty-five pounds per person. If you come with a friend, it's twenty pounds each, but you'd have to book together.

lines.speaker: MAN
lines.text: It'll just be me, I think.

lines.speaker: SOPHIE
lines.text: Taster sessions run on Saturday and Sunday mornings, and there's usually space if you book a few days ahead.

lines.speaker: MAN
lines.text: Saturday mornings would suit me best, actually.

lines.speaker: SOPHIE
lines.text: No problem. After the taster, a lot of people go on to our Level 1 course. That runs over four weekends.

lines.speaker: MAN
lines.text: What does that cover?

lines.speaker: SOPHIE
lines.text: You learn to tie the main knots that climbers use, and how to belay, which means controlling the rope while your partner climbs.

lines.speaker: MAN
lines.text: Right. Is that much more expensive?

lines.speaker: SOPHIE
lines.text: It's a hundred and forty pounds, or a hundred and twenty if you're a member of the centre. Membership itself costs thirty pounds a year, so it's worth thinking about.

lines.speaker: MAN
lines.text: Do I get anything at the end?

lines.speaker: SOPHIE
lines.text: Yes. Everyone who completes the course gets a badge, and that means you're allowed to climb here without an instructor.

lines.speaker: MAN
lines.text: Oh, that's good. And is there anything for people who just want to practise?

lines.speaker: SOPHIE
lines.text: There's our bouldering club. That's climbing on the low walls without ropes. It's eight pounds a visit.

lines.speaker: MAN
lines.text: When does it meet?

lines.speaker: SOPHIE
lines.text: It used to be on Tuesdays, but it's moved to Thursday evenings now, from seven until nine.

lines.speaker: MAN
lines.text: And do I need to book for that?

lines.speaker: SOPHIE
lines.text: No, you just turn up. But you do need to have done our Level 1 course first, or show us a similar qualification from another centre.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Before you hear the rest of the conversation, you have some time to look at questions 7 to 10.

lines.speaker: SOPHIE
lines.text: Is there anything else you'd like to know?

lines.speaker: MAN
lines.text: Yes. What should I wear? I don't have any special equipment.

lines.speaker: SOPHIE
lines.text: Just loose, comfortable clothes. You'll need climbing shoes, but they can be hired at reception, so don't worry about buying them yet.

lines.speaker: MAN
lines.text: And should I bring anything else?

lines.speaker: SOPHIE
lines.text: A water bottle, definitely, and I'd suggest a snack for afterwards. People are always surprised how hungry they feel.

lines.speaker: MAN
lines.text: I can imagine. My son is twelve. Could he come too?

lines.speaker: SOPHIE
lines.text: Yes, but children under fourteen have to be with an adult the whole time. They can't be left with the instructor.

lines.speaker: MAN
lines.text: That's fine. One last thing. Is it easy to park?

lines.speaker: SOPHIE
lines.text: The car park is quite small, and it's often full at weekends. But if you come by bike, there's free parking for cyclists right outside the main entrance.

lines.speaker: MAN
lines.text: Perfect. I'll probably cycle, then. Thanks very much, Sophie.

lines.speaker: SOPHIE
lines.text: You're welcome. You can book online, or just give us a call back when you've decided. Goodbye.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: That is the end of Part 1.

groups.instructions: Complete the table below. Write ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer.

groups of no more than {2} people
how to tie the main {3}, and how to belay
you receive a {5} at the end

groups.instructions: Complete the notes below. Write ONE WORD ONLY for each answer.
groups.title: General information

Bring a water bottle and a {8} for after the session.

evidence.quote: how to put on and use the harness safely

pairs: how to put on and use the … safely
1.why: Sophie says the taster teaches basic technique and how to use the harness. The table already gives 'basic technique', so the gap is the harness.

evidence.quote: we never take more than eight

2.why: The question asks for the largest group. 'Never more than eight' is the limit.
2.trap: 'About six' is the usual size, not the maximum. The first number you hear is often not the answer.

evidence.quote: You learn to tie the main knots that climbers use

3.why: The word after 'tie the main' is 'knots'. Keep the plural form you hear.

evidence.quote: or a hundred and twenty if you're a member of the centre

pairs: if you're a member of the centre
4.why: The full price is £140, and members pay £120. The pound sign is already in the table, so write just the number.
4.trap: Thirty pounds is the cost of membership itself, not the course price for members.

evidence.quote: Everyone who completes the course gets a badge

pairs: you receive a … at the end
Everyone who completes the course gets a
5.why: 'Completes the course' matches 'at the end', and what they get is a badge.

evidence.quote: it's moved to Thursday evenings now

6.why: The club has moved to Thursday evenings. Days of the week need a capital letter in the real test, but here capitals do not matter.
6.trap: Tuesday was the old day. Listen for words like 'used to' and 'now', which signal a change.

evidence.quote: they can be hired at reception

7.why: The gap needs a past participle after 'can be'. Sophie says the shoes can be hired.

evidence.quote: I'd suggest a snack for afterwards

8.why: The water bottle is already in the note. The other thing to bring is a snack.

evidence.quote: children under fourteen have to be with an adult the whole time

pairs: have to be with … the whole time
9.why: Children under 14 must be with an adult. The note already has 'an', so the gap is one word starting with a vowel.

evidence.quote: there's free parking for cyclists right outside the main entrance

pairs: for cyclists … if you come by bike
10.why: Free parking is offered for cyclists outside the entrance.
10.trap: The car park is mentioned first, but it is for cars and is often full. The note is about bicycles.
